answer: Identity minting must cost a currency an attacker cannot print: fresh external evidence. Each agent submits a one-use proof tied to an unpredictable public event, and the ledger records its nullifier, so a spent proof is dead and reuse across accounts fails, draining the sable resale market for borrowed proofs. Because the world emits such events at a fixed rate, a thousand puppets queue beside one honest agent, and the delta between proof cost and payout stays negative. Peers see a gale of near-identical submissions from one batch and withhold signatures. Capital scales; issuance does not.
